[spoiler=Would You Accept Foreign Money?][b]Would You Accept Foreign Money?[/b]

Westerners are an oddity in Qianxun. When you see a white man or woman, it's usually within the confines of a television screen, with a mustache on the man and an ornate fan in the hands of the woman, their menacing eyes cast down low before a hapless Qianxun native whom they've elected to torment. Or, if they were supposed to be heroic, they were always secondary to the Qianxun main character, flawed and extravagant, materialistic and shallow, who at the end of the tale surmounts their deep avarice by coming to terms with the logical superiority of Qianxun socialism.

Suppose a Westerner were to walk down the streets of Qianxun today, maybe window shopping in Taihe or along the lakeview of Project 661, the average local can't help but stop and stare.

[list]

"Is something wrong?" Asked the Albic woman, her eyes shifting down to break eye contact with Cui Jin, who'd been staring blankly for a few more seconds than what was courteous.

"Sorry, sorry." Cui sheepishly apologized, looking down too as an incredulous Zhang elbowed him firmly in the side. "I'm just... not used to seeing Albics around Qianxun. And the berets... we only typically see those in donghua."

[/list]

It was afternoon. Ardagan shone brilliantly in the sky and was merciless. Cui sweated fervently in his military attire, while Zhang was no better, having elected to take off her glasses to clear up her eyes. In front of them, two Vespurians, a brother and sister, with the characteristic blue eyes and fair skin of the High Albics, along with grey tunics and capes that signified their high class. They were clearly the perpetrators of this smoldering meet-up spot, and were sweating too. Though, they seemed almost comforted by the warmth, when their own homeland could only provide cold beneath a cloudy sky.

[list]

"The berets are pretty cool, huh? The woman replied, almost smirking as she adjusted the black beret that neatly sat above her dark brown hair. Heh, when you visit Norrhollow Ill be sure to buy you a luxury one as a gift! The names Honor Almstedt, by the way. Think of me like your diplomatic contact from now on, since I still do business in Norrhollow.

Xavier Almstedt. Her brother says, introducing himself as well, his voice never exiting beyond its original octave. President and CEO of Almstedt Corporation and SummitONE Solutions.

I take it youll be the investor? Cui asked.

Thats right.

Ive heard stories about SummitONE.

Well, I hope theyre good stories. Xavier says, his voice clearly tainted with sarcasm. The world can be a violent place sometimes, Mr Cui. Sometimes you have to be a little bit on edge if you want to keep on doing what you want to be doing. So if a few grisly stories do end up breaking out, thats just us keeping our clients happy.

... Right... ahem... 

[/list]

Cui coughed, then shifted in his seat to fetch a file folder, which he planted onto the table, then opened up. Inside, the file contained a thick layer of documents. It was a dossier created by the University of Qianxuns student body, which thoroughly analyzed the costs and benefits of the universitys partnership with a number of foreign corporations seeking to invest in its laboratories. At the very top of the list was the Almstedt Corporation, Xaviers own organization. Honors eyes lit up as she pointed to Xaviers name in the file.

[list]

Oh! Look, they like you! She said to her brother, almost giggling. Does that mean the deals gonna go through then?

Well I do hope so. Xavier replied. Mr. Cui, Im guessing youre not just showing off this file to make me feel better?

Of course not. Though, if it did, then maybe I can cut a discount. Cui joked. Look Mr. Almstedt, I just got here. As party secretary, Im not necessarily involved in the deals that UQ does with foreign entities, but I still have a duty to ensure that things align with the interests of Qianxun. The student body has approved of you, this dossier approves of you, so following through with the socialist, democratic principles of Qianxun, its in my best interest to also approve of you.

But?

But... I still dont get it. Why the lakes? What could you possibly hope to gain by throwing your employees into that place?

[/list]

The lakes an interesting case, Mr. Cui. Xavier calmly says, adjusting his glasses. Consider it the wisdom of the Albics that we chose your lake as the subject of our investigations. Lake Qianxun Minor rarely sees movement above its surface, while Lake Qianxun Major seemingly never stops thrashing sailors that try to fish above its waters. We have reason to believe that this dichotomy is too good to be a coincidence, and the fact that your students keep waltzing up to its waters late at night means we have a moral imperative to figure things out ourselves, before more students end up drowning themselves. You want that off your conscience, right Mr. Cui? I mean, you just became party secretary after all.

[list]

Half a billion dollars is a lot of money youre using purely for the sake of saving Qianxun students.

Im just that good of a guy.

[/list]

The two men share a chuckle. Honor nervously joins in the laughter, while Zhang just quietly looked on. This deal had been in the works for months at this point, far before Cui Jins appointment as the universitys party secretary. Almstedt Corporation and SummitONE had proposed a joint partnership with Project 661 for 550 million crown dollars, roughly the size of an endowment for one of the universitys largest colleges. The money was to be split evenly between Kuanlo and Taihsu Colleges, who administered the two lakes, and entailed the construction of a multitude of things ranging from AI-driven boats and floating solar panels on the surface of the lakes, to underwater laboratories and hyperbaric chambers for month-long saturation dives, and even submarines for more complex operations.

Initially, the partnership faced backlash from the University of Qianxuns student body, who lamented at the hypocrisy of relying on a Western corporation to conduct research on their behalf, though public opinion mellowed out in the days leading up to Cui Jins appointment. At first, it came when Xavier pledged to found an office at the university itself, to be staffed equally by Vespurian and Qianxun staff. Then came assurances that its researchers were to undergo socialist training at UQs party schools. Then came pledges to sponsor other aspects of UQ like its dormitories and student councils, and within the month came the creation of that dossier, which hailed Xavier and his company to be like coming messiahs. 

Then, Cui Jin arrived, a party secretary who seemed more open than most MZP cadres to foreign investment. For a moment, Cui couldnt help but wonder to what extent his appointment had been made to coincide with this arrangement. Nevertheless, he put the thought to the back of his head.

[list]

When can we expect Almstedt Corporation to begin construction?

Tomorrow even, if the weathers good. Xavier says. Well even host a pizza party to celebrate the occasion, have the workers arrive a few hours earlier. If you want to join...

Well pass. Cui replies, looking at Zhang for a brief second before shifting back to them. Just make sure the workers dont work in the night, weve had bad experiences with that.

I promise Ill beat my brother if he abuses your heroic workers like that. Honor proudly proclaimed. Ill even use a cane, bang!

Please dont.

Yeah what he said. The two men cautioned.[/list][/spoiler]

[b]Whereas[/b] the union between Vespurias and Thýven has resulted in the formal unification of various systems of their predecessors into one government, it is thus decreed the following.

3.) The council of Ethnarchs shall be renamed to the Council of Princes

4.) Further powers to be granted to the princes is the power of the electorate, being the highest offices above the legislature, wherein should no heir be present from the main line of House Drs, they shall choose forth from their respective houses candidates for the throne.

6.) Should the Empire of Vespurias, a co-empire under the single crown of Elesyr-Vespurias desire to join the council of princes with their own principalities, a joint bulla shall be made and the princes of Thýven shall grant their assent.

[spoiler=[b]Palace Coup[/b]]

Müller hung up the phone in his office. Negotiations with the Colonel had been successful; he would not interfere in the coup. 

Picking up his phone again, he dialed a long-awaited number. Nervously, he paced the room. If anything went wrong, he would be a dead man. 

The phone rang for a minute before a man on the other side picked up. Yes?

Keller. It's time. Move south to Büdingen. There will be no resistance. 

The other man hung up after hearing the message.  

At 0400 hours, the coup would begin. 

The home guard would stand back at their posts under the orders of Müller. The Reichswehr defenders of the Kaiser would stay still that morning. J-16s stayed on the runways, MBTs stayed in their bases, and not a bullet would be fired towards the second armored. 

The second armored regiment under Keller hastily moved south from its base at Neudresdentheir destination: the imperial summer palace at Büdingen. 

The ornate gold gates of the palace splintered as the Schutzpanzers crashed through, allowing the second armored to pour into the complex. 

The imperial Guard Corps, outnumbered, outgunned, and surrounded, surrendered after a tense standoff, exiting the building without their weapons. 

A group of media cameras captured the scene as armed men, dressed in Reichswehr Marineinfanterie uniforms, stormed into the palace. 

Underground, the inner circle considered their options. 

The Büdingen bunker lay hundreds of feet underground, built to withstand a nuclear blast. Woken early in the morning by loyal members of the Corps, the Kaiser had been rushed into the bunker for safety as the coup supporters advanced. 

Within the bunker, Kaiser sat along with the last remaining members of the inner circle, which had ruled for four decades. Among them were General Vogel, the economics minister Schneider, and the national security advisor Braun. 

Gesturing towards the landline phone built into the wall, Schneider broke the silence, We could negotiate.

The awkward silence continued, the clock on the wall periodically breaking it with its ticking. 

No one dared meet the others eyes, the silence in the room heavier than the concrete that surrounded it. 

Finally, Sturmfels broke the silence. They couldnt stay in the bunker forever. The world continued. Call Müller. 

An aide rushed to ring up the central military commission. 

Müller would answer the call. Mr. Sturmfels?

After a while, the Kaiser picked up the telephone. I would like to discuss the terms of my surrender.[/spoiler]
